claim: The proof of `commutator_sup_left` detours through the quotient `(H ⊔ K ⊔ N) ⧸ (⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆)`. That needs a separate private helper `commutator_sup_left'`, five `have`s for containment in `M`, `subgroupOf` transport with `convert`, and two large `simp` calls. The key fact it establishes, that `H ⊔ K` normalises `⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆`, already gives the result by closure induction on `H ⊔ K`, with the existing `commutatorElement_mul_left_eq_conj_mul` and `commutatorElement_inv_left` identities.
requested_change:
Prove `commutator_sup_left` directly and delete the private `commutator_sup_left'`:
theorem commutator_sup_left (H K N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] : ⁅H ⊔ K, N⁆ = ⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆ := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_
    (sup_le (commutator_mono_left le_sup_left) (commutator_mono_left le_sup_right))
  have hX : ⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆ ≤ N := sup_le (commutator_le_right H N) (commutator_le_right K N)
  have hHK : H ⊔ K ≤ normalizer (⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆ : Subgroup G) := sup_le
    (by grw [le_normalizer_iff_commutator_le_right, hX, ← le_sup_left])
    (by grw [le_normalizer_iff_commutator_le_right, hX, ← le_sup_right])
  rw [sup_eq_closure H K] at hHK
  rw [commutator_le]
  intro g hg
  rw [sup_eq_closure H K] at hg
  induction hg using closure_induction with
  | mem x hx =>
    rcases hx with hx | hx
    · exact fun n hn ↦ mem_sup_left (commutator_mem_commutator hx hn)
    · exact fun n hn ↦ mem_sup_right (commutator_mem_commutator hx hn)
  | one => simp
  | mul x y hx hy ihx ihy =>
    intro n hn
    rw [commutatorElement_mul_left_eq_conj_mul]
    exact mul_mem ((mem_normalizer_iff.mp (hHK hx) _).mp (ihy n hn)) (ihx n hn)
  | inv x hx ihx =>
    intro n hn
    rw [commutatorElement_inv_left, ← commutatorElement_inv]
    exact (mem_normalizer_iff''.mp (hHK hx) _).mp (inv_mem (ihx n hn))

The direct proof uses neither `commutator_sup_left'`, `commutator_le_of_le`, `subgroupOf`, `convert` nor `inf_normalizer_le_normalizer_sup`.
